title: Coming of age
hookLine: the pen is lifted from the child, until one day it isn't

cards: For years a child prays beside a parent, copies the bows, maybe tries a half-day fast in Ramadan to see what it's like. All of it is real, and all of it is welcome.

And yet, in Islamic teaching, there's a line waiting up ahead. One day, with no ceremony required, the child crosses it. A hadith describes the time before that line with a striking picture: the pen is lifted.

teach.h: THE PEN IS LIFTED FROM THREE.
teach.b: Here's the hadith, in Sunan Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi, in paraphrase: the pen is lifted from three.

From the sleeper until he wakes, from the child until he reaches maturity, and from the one who has lost his reason until he recovers it. Commentators read the pen as the one that records a person's deeds against them.
Before maturity, nothing is yet written against a child. Childhood is protected time. But protected isn't empty.
In Sahih Muslim, in paraphrase, a woman on the pilgrimage lifts up a small child and asks the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: does he have a Hajj? He answers: yes, and you have a reward.
A child's good deeds are welcomed. Second, the word.
Taklif means being given a charge, a responsibility. A person who has reached it is called mukallaf: one who is now responsible.
Scholars set out the signs of maturity, and the schools differ on the details, but the idea is shared: at maturity, the duties begin. Prayer, fasting, the rest. Now it counts.
Third, the charge comes with a limit.

The Qur'an says, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." In Arabic, that verse's verb is yukallifu, from the same root as taklif. The charge and its limit, in one sentence.
Fourth, look back at the years before. The khatm, the prayers beside a parent, the half fasts: none of it was required.
It was practice, freely given. Taklif doesn't erase that. It builds on it.
The child who already knows the movements walks into responsibility already holding them.

how: In Islamic law, a person becomes mukallaf at maturity, and from then on prayer, fasting and the other duties are required of them; before that, children are encouraged to practice and their good deeds are welcomed.

games.why: yes, and you have a reward (Sahih Muslim). the pen of duty is lifted from a child, but good deeds are still welcomed.

practice: Recall a moment when something in your life started to count, a first job, a key of your own, a promise that was yours to keep, and name one responsibility you carry now that fits you, not one beyond your scope.
Then let this part of the path pass by: the call in the ear, the date, the name, the 'aqiqah, the hair, khitan, prayer at seven, the khatm, and now taklif. A whole childhood.

wordCard.voice: Taklif. Being given a charge: at maturity, the duties of the faith begin, and none beyond a soul's scope. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a charge laid on someone; religious responsibility.

carryVoice: Your line: now it counts. A charge, and never one beyond your scope. Rest well, and come back tomorrow.
